name: Diprosopus (Craniofacial Duplication)

criteria.description: Presence of partial or complete duplication of facial structures
Associated cranial malformations such as hypertelorism or cleft palate
Radiologic evidence of duplicated facial bones and soft tissues
Exclusion of conjoined twinning by clinical and imaging evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of facial duplication confirmed clinically and by imaging, with exclusion of conjoined twinning
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be inconclusive.

common.symptomName: Non-midline cleft of the upper lip

laboratory: Generally nonspecific; supportive labs for associated anomalies
imaging: CT or MRI demonstrating duplication of facial bones and soft tissues
Ultrasound for prenatal diagnosis showing facial duplication
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases
Possible involvement of SHH (Sonic Hedgehog) pathway abnormalities
other: Prenatal ultrasound may detect facial duplication
Postnatal clinical examination is critical for diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of two separate bodies fused at the head or torso
Distinct cardiac activity in each twin
Unilateral or bilateral facial clefts without duplication

redFlags: Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
references: Cohen MM Jr. Craniofacial duplication (diprosopus): a review. Am J Med Genet. 1990
Jones KL. Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation. 7th ed. 2013
